symptom: describe page printed MDL that did not parse ("no viable alternative at input") for a page whose documentation held a CSS comment ending in `*/`.
cause: The lexer ends a DOC_COMMENT at the first `*/`. Eleven describe paths built `/** … */` by hand with no escape; only writeDocumentDocComment (#1510) and three property-clause fallbacks handled `*/`, by not stating the text at all.
fix: doccomment.Escape writes `*/` as `*\/` (a `*`, any backslash run, `/` gains one backslash); extractDocComment applies Unescape. Every hand-built emitter and outputJavadocIndented go through Escape.
insight: Grep for the emitters, not the doctype: the reported page was one of eleven hand-rolled `/**` writers. A `--` fallback that states nothing is only safe where the create path carries stored documentation; a nested element (an attribute) has no such carry, so a lossless escape is the fix that holds everywhere.
test: mdl/executor/doc_comment_comment_end_2113_test.go (entity, attribute, microflow round trips through the parser); mdl/doccomment/doccomment_test.go
